fields.title: 1. Event — Cross-checking the Flight 15 '11/13 double catch' reports against primary sources
fields.md:
| Item | Value (checked 2026-11-10) | Source grade · source |
|---|---|---|
| LL2 launch record | **NET 2026-11-13 22:45 UTC** · status 'To Be Confirmed' · window end 2026-11-14 00:00 UTC · last updated 2026-11-09 23:06 UTC · Orbital Launch Pad 2 (Starbase). Mission description (pre-launch planning wording): first attempt at second-stage return to the launch site · booster tower catch | ④ [LL2 upcoming](https://ll.thespacedevs.com/2.3.0/launches/upcoming/?search=Starship&limit=3&mode=normal) · `data/spacex_watch.json launches.starship_next` (11/10 08:31 KST, same date and status) |
| Origin of the date | SpaceX launch vice president Dontchev (UP.Summit) gave 11/13. The earlier FAA flight plan slide went from 11/8 → 11/12 — **it is a regulator planning date, not a company date** | ⑥ [Teslarati 11/05](https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-starship-catch-nov-13/) (citing Ars Technica) |
| Hardware | Booster 22 33-engine static fire (10/25) · Ship 42 6-engine static fire of about 60 seconds (around 10/27) — same as the November issue and the 11/9 run record (no change) | ⑥ [Teslarati 11/05](https://www.teslarati.com/spacex-starship-catch-nov-13/) · `state.triggers_next_12m[T3].status` |
| FAA license | **Issuance of a modified Flight 15 license is not confirmed** — reports say the Flight 14 license covered only that flight, and that a modification is needed to include the Ship's return to the launch site (flight over densely populated areas). The FAA Starship page returned 403 in this run | ⑤ [NASASpaceflight November](https://www.nasaspaceflight.com/2026/11/starship-flight-15-awaits-faa/) (title and search summary — body 403) · [FAA Starship](https://www.faa.gov/space/stakeholder_engagement/spacex_starship) (403) |
| Filings | **No SpaceX 8-K or IR release** — latest on EDGAR is the 11/06 8-K (Item 5.02); latest on IR RSS is 11/06 | ① [EDGAR filing list](https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001181412.json) · ② [IR RSS](https://ir.spacex.com/rss/pressrelease.aspx), accessed 2026-11-10 |

**Verdict**: The content of the two watcher reports (11/13 · simultaneous booster + Ship catch) is **the same** as the T3 record in the 11/9 run. The only new confirmation is that LL2 kept the date as of the evening of 11/9 (UTC), and the remaining uncertainty (the license) is unchanged. Since this is a **confirmation**, not an event, there is no milestone or probability input — B-2027-1 (start of Ship recovery and reuse) and R2 move only once the flight result is out. The measurement layer LL2 will automatically detect it as a 'flight with confirmed result' (`launch_final`), and that opens the next event run (Source: table above · `state.probability_adjustment_rules` R2 · `state.milestones` B-2027-1).

**Measurement layer's share (listing only)**: The watcher woke the engine again with a repeat report of the same trigger and the same date. The judgment layer had nothing to do — a rule not to wake it for a 'repeat report of a date already recorded' is left in `open_questions_for_next_run` as a measurement-layer design task (Source: `data/spacex_watch.json` due).
